name: Gabe Evans

summary.text: Gabe Evans is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Colorado's 8th Congressional District, first elected in 2024.

He served about twelve years in the U.S. Army and Colorado Army National Guard as a UH-60 Black Hawk helicopter pilot, including a combat deployment to the Middle East, and spent over a decade as an Arvada police officer before serving two years in the Colorado House of Representatives.
He and his wife own and operate a family farm in southern Weld County.

experience.text: U.S. House of Representatives, Colorado's 8th District, since January 3, 2025.
Arvada Police Department, police officer/lieutenant, over ten years.
U.S. Army and Colorado Army National Guard, UH-60 Black Hawk helicopter pilot and company commander, 2007-2019, including a combat deployment to the Middle East.

record.title: Stop Pills that Kill Act
record.detail: Would implement new penalties and close a sentencing loophole for counterfeit fentanyl-laced pill production; passed House Energy and Commerce Committee.

record.title: STOP (Strengthening Tools of Oversight to Prevent) Medicaid Fraud Act
record.detail: Would require states to electronically verify certain Medicaid-funded services (non-emergency transport, applied behavior analysis) were provided before payment. Its stated aim is reducing Medicaid fraud.

record.title: H.R. 1679, Global Investment in American Jobs Act of 2025
record.detail: Sponsor, with Rep. Robin Kelly (D-IL) as cosponsor. The bill directs the Secretary of Commerce to conduct an interagency review of, and report to Congress on, ways to increase U.S. competitiveness in attracting foreign direct investment. His office reports the House passed the bill on June 23, 2025.

record.title: HB24-1313, Housing in Transit-Oriented Communities, House third reading
record.detail: Voted No. The bill passed the House 37-24 (4 excused) and was signed into law May 13, 2024.

record.title: H.R. 1834, Breaking the Gridlock Act (extension of enhanced ACA premium tax credits), passage
record.detail: Voted Nay. The bill extends the enhanced premium tax credit under Internal Revenue Code section 36B through 2028; it passed the House 230-196.

positions.source_title: Congressman Gabe Evans' Stop Pills that Kill Act Clears Committee, Heads to House Floor
positions.quote: The Stop Pills that Kill Act would implement new penalties and close a sentencing loophole for counterfeit pill production.
positions.note: Sponsored a federal bill adding penalties for counterfeit pill production, which supports tougher fentanyl penalties without reaching Proposition 132's mandatory prison for selling any amount. The release says combating fentanyl is a top legislative priority for him.

positions.source_title: Border Security and Immigration - Gabe Evans
positions.quote: It is an issue that hits close to home because Colorado’s sanctuary state policies have led to the presence of cartels and illegal criminals gangs like Tren de Aragua.
positions.note: Criticizes Colorado's sanctuary-state policies limiting cooperation with federal immigration enforcement; typo ("criminals gangs") preserved verbatim from source.

positions.source_title: Border Security and Immigration - Gabe Evans
positions.quote: There are many aspects of the immigration system that need fixing, but my priorities are: secure the physical border, streamline the system for legal immigration, and deport illegal immigrants who commit crimes.
positions.note: Prioritizes deporting immigrants who commit crimes specifically, rather than all people without legal status, so coded as agree-with-qualification rather than strongest value.

positions.quote: I voted for the largest tax cut in American history, including no tax on tips, overtime, or social security—saving Colorado families over $4,000 a year.
positions.note: From his 2026 Candidate Connection survey response; reinforced by his recorded Yea vote on H.R. 1 final passage (clerk.house.gov/Votes/2025190, 2025-07-03).

positions.quote: This is also why I support free market policies, which will allow good competition and bring down costs.
positions.note: Supports free-market policies to bring down prescription drug costs; opposition to expanded government coverage is inferred from that, and matches his vote for H.R. 1, which added Medicaid work requirements.

positions.quote: I support increasing domestic production of energy resources to ensure our energy independence and end our reliance on foreign countries. Supporting projects like the Keystone XL Pipeline and domestic drilling is necessary to the overall health of our country.
positions.note: Statement also voices support for renewables as part of an "all of the above" approach, so coded as disagree-with-qualification rather than the strongest value.
